summary: Two fixes for Sort By in search results, in one commit. (A) Result rows have their Date Created, Date Last Opened and Permissions: new `FileEntry::read_metadata` (created, mode, readonly; the entry is left alone when the file can't be read), `SearchRequest.full_metadata` and `.last_opened`, read in a new `finish` step after the cut, so at most `limit` reads. The window asks only while a column, the groups or the results' sort goes by them (`wants_result_metadata`, `wants_result_last_opened` in src/finder/list.rs) and searches again when such a need appears (toggle_column, set_group_by, adopt_settings for a column added in another tab, set_sort). (B) A sort says which items a cut list holds. `SearchRequest.sort`: the engine makes the list it makes without the sort first, and `SearchResponse.sort_chooses` says of it whether a sort may choose its items. Only then does it fetch wide (20,000 per search location), put the hits in the sort's order (`sort_before_cut`, mirroring `listing::compare`) and cut. A search with unquoted words is sorted among the hits that have every word in their name, and only when the cut list holds nothing but such names and more of them match than fit; a list with a loose match in it, or with a best match that was opened from this search before, stays the best matches and is not searched again. Searches with loose text no name is held to (`main.rs:42`, alone or beside words; a lone `src/`) are never sorted before the cut (`loose_text`). Dates the index lacks (Date Created, Date Last Opened, a folder's Date Modified) are read for the 5,000 best-ranked hits that need them. The engine's answer stays best first; the window sorts its rows itself and re-runs the search on a sort change only when the answer on screen says a sort chooses. Also: results found from Recents, the Trash or a results view are sorted when Name ascending is chosen (`keep_order` leaves searches out).
changelog: Sorting search results only reordered the items already listed, so with more matches than **Results shown** the largest or newest ones could be missing: `*.log` by Size gave the largest of an arbitrary 500. When a search finds more than it lists, a sort now chooses among every match, up to 20,000 in each search location. For unquoted words, which match loosely, it chooses among the items that have every word in their name, when the list holds nothing else and more of them match than fit; otherwise the list stays the best matches, in the new order. In search results the Date Created and Date Last Opened columns were blank, Permissions said `read-write` for every file, sorting by Date Created sorted by name, and groups by either date put everything under No Date. They now show what the files have, read from the disk for the items listed while a column, the sort, or the groups use them. A search made from Recents is now sorted when you choose Name.
behaviour_changes: Cut result list (status bar shows `+`) of a name search without unquoted words (globs, extensions, kinds, quoted words, folder filters, exclusions, one-letter searches): choosing Name, Date Modified, Date Created, Size, Kind, a Folder or Date Last Opened header, or the other direction, runs the search again, and the list becomes the first Results-shown of every match in that order (up to 20,000 per search location). Seen in the window: `*.txt` with Results shown 8 in the demo folder lists notes.txt (77 bytes), Project Atlas.txt, readme.txt first, where the unsorted eight are 9-byte files.

Cut list of a search with unquoted words, when every listed item has every word in its name (letters in a row) and more such names match than fit: the same, chosen among the names that have every word. Seen: `tax` with Results shown 2 lists the two largest of the three names with tax in them. In a 77,559-file tree, 40 of the 111 searches tried are of this kind (readme, test, log, mod, lib, ...), 3 list every match, and 68 are of the kind below.

Cut list of a search with unquoted words that has anything else in it (a match by the path alone, or a file opened from this search before that ranks first though its name lacks a word): a sort only reorders the rows on screen, with no search, exactly as before this change. The same for a search with text matched loosely that isn't a word names are checked for: a word with a line suffix (`main.rs:42`, `meeting 10:30`), alone or beside other words, and a folder name typed alone (`src/`).

The re-run after a sort change is not a new search: the rows keep the selection by path and the scroll position. A selected item that the new list no longer holds loses its selection (the largest 500 of all matches need not include the best match that was selected). The status bar spinner shows meanwhile.
Going back to Relevance on a list a sort chose searches again and lists the best matches. On any other list it takes no search.

A list that was not cut: no new search and the same items, as before. Exception: Sort By Date Created (or the Date Last Opened header) runs one search to read the dates, when nothing shown had them read already.
Choosing the direction (Ascending, Descending) that the results already have searches nothing again, as before this change.

Date Created and Date Last Opened columns are filled for name-search results; Permissions shows `rw-r--r--` instead of `read-write` on Unix, and `read-only` for read-only files on Windows. Sort by Date Created sorts by date instead of by name. Group By Date Created or Date Last Opened groups by date instead of putting every file under No Date.
Adding one of those columns or choosing such groups during a name search runs it again, in every tab that is searching (the column setting is shared between tabs).
While such a column is shown, each name search reads up to Results shown files from the disk (5,000 with a Nushell filter on). Without one, a search reads nothing more than before.
A search made from Recents, the Trash or a results view, sorted by Name ascending, is now sorted. That includes contents searches made there.

Cost. A search under a non-Relevance sort is one engine pass unless its list is one a sort chooses, then two (the second wide). Debug build, shared CPU, 77,559 files in four search locations: plain 40 to 110 ms; under a sort that doesn't choose the same (the implementer's version took 150 to 400 ms there, for the same list); under a sort that chooses 150 to 650 ms. fff-search is built optimised in the dev profile, so the rest is fffinder-core's own unoptimised code; release is unmeasured (the guide forbids --release).

A sort by Date Created, Date Last Opened, or Date Modified where folders match, reads at most 5,000 hits from the disk (or Results shown, if that is more) to choose: every hit for the first two, the folders for the third. The best-ranked are read and the sort goes without the rest. With a filter on (limit 5,000) a Date Created or Date Last Opened sort therefore always ends with the unsorted list.

API: `SearchRequest.sort`, `.full_metadata`, `.last_opened` (all default off); `SearchResponse.sort_chooses`; `FileEntry::read_metadata`. With `sort` set the hits still come back best first; the sort only chooses which hits the limit lets in, and `sort_chooses` in the answer says whether it did. `/v1/find`, `fff find` and `fff open` are unchanged (the server's request literal got `..Default::default()`).
Manual: the sort paragraph of "Sorting and hidden files" and one sentence in "Ranking and limits".
left_out: Searches with unquoted words whose cut list has a loose match in it stay the best matches under a sort, by design; so do searches where the wide fetch would find more names than the plain list holds (`x86` in the test tree: 394 names and 106 path matches listed, 563 names matching). The manual says when a sort chooses.
Contents-search rows still have no last-opened date, and a contents search still sorts only the files it lists (verifier: out of scope).
Recents itself still has blank Date Created and Permissions: `Engine::recents` goes through the same `into_hit` and has no request to ask with (verifier: out of scope).

`is_symlink` is not filled for results (plan A.1 asked for it): no column shows it, and its only reader, the LS_COLORS name styles, would colour a result differently depending on which columns are shown.

Name searches still can't be cancelled: a superseded search under a sort that chooses runs both passes to the end. The abort flag is made for every search in run_search (see cancel-content-search's record) but `Engine::search` takes none.
A one-letter or quoted search under a sort that chooses fetches wide twice, the same fetch both times. Sharing it would mean taking `Engine::search` apart; not done.
CHANGELOG.md: the guide forbids it. The entry is in the commit message and in this record.
README.md and the Search Syntax dialog: nothing there states what changed.
Release-build timing: the guide forbids --release. Debug numbers are under behaviour_changes.

Not compiled for macOS or Windows. No cfg-gated code is touched; `read_metadata` uses `unix_mode`, which exists under both cfgs; src/term, src/macos.rs and src/win.rs use nothing that changed (grepped), so clippy --features term was not run. The new engine test with `track_open` is `#[cfg(not(windows))]` like its two neighbours that open a file from a search.

review_fixes: A sort click on a cut list whose sort can't choose replaced the rows with another run of the search. The plain search is not the same from run to run where many matches tie (see Found, not fixed), so the click changed which items were listed for no reason: in the 77,559-file tree two runs of `index` share 265 to 396 of 500 items, `bench` about 300, and a selected item among the rest lost its selection. Before this improvement a sort click only reordered rows. Fix: `SearchResponse.sort_chooses`, kept in `SearchStats`; `result_sort_changed` searches again only when the answer on screen says a sort chooses (it went by `truncated`). UI test a_list_with_loose_matches_in_it_keeps_its_items_under_a_sort.

A sort dropped the search's best match when that was a file opened from this search before whose name lacks a word. fff-search gives that file +1,000, so it ranks first wherever the word is in its path, and `sort_before_cut` keeps to the names with the words. Reproduced on the implementer's commit: after `track_open(ledger/summary.pdf, "ledger")` the file is the best match (score 1051) and the largest match of all, and Size descending listed my-ledger-notes.txt and xledgerx.txt without it. Fix: `sort_can_choose` looks at the list the search makes without the sort; with any hit in it whose name lacks a word, the list is left to the ranking. Engine test a_best_match_opened_before_stays_in_the_list_under_a_sort.

The same check saves the wide fetch where a sort has nothing to choose. The implementer's engine fetched 20,000 per location and ranked them on every search under a sort whose list was cut, then threw the result away when the names with the words didn't fill the list: 66 of the 111 searches tried in the test tree, 150 to 400 ms each in place of 40 to 90 ms (debug). Now those return after the plain pass. Cost: a search whose plain list has path matches in it though more names match further down fff-search's ranking is no longer sorted among the names (`x86`, `a b`: 2 of the 42 the implementer's version sorted).

Loose text beside a word was sorted through. The rule "a word with a line suffix is never sorted before the cut" held only when it was the whole search (`words.is_empty() && loose`): `ledger txt:7` with Results shown 2 listed the two largest names with ledger in them and dropped the best match ledger.txt, though `txt` is matched anywhere along the path. Fix: `loose_text` compares what fff-search matches loosely with the search's words, and any such text that isn't one of them leaves the list to the ranking. Unit test text_matched_loosely_is_told_from_the_words_and_the_filters, and `ledger txt:7` in the fixture test.

A sort by Date Modified read every matching folder's date from the disk with no bound: up to 20,000 per search location on every search under that sort, on a thread that can't be stopped. The verifier's bound was applied to Date Created and Date Last Opened only. Now a folder's date counts as a read like those (`CutKey::reads_disk`): the 5,000 best-ranked folders are read, every file is still sorted by the index's date. On a local disk the reads were not measurable (12,685 folders: same time as a sort by Size); the bound is for slow volumes.
`set_ascending` with the direction the results already have re-ran the search on a cut list (the Sort menu's checked item can be clicked). It now does nothing, as before the improvement.

When a search made with a sort finds that the names all fit after all (or the read bound left too few), the answer says `sort_chooses: false`, so the window stops re-running that search on further sort changes.

Comment and doc corrections that go with the above: `set_aside` in `cut_in_order` also covers hits past the read bound; the manual's sort paragraph says when a list is left as it is and what is read for the 5,000 best-ranked; the commit message was rewritten for the final behaviour.
notes:
Checked. check.sh on the trunk commit 26ab60c: CHECK OK, 562 passed in 16 test binaries, 3/3 known root-only failures. The trunk had moved three times since the implementer's base 9cf7635 (69b956f history-menus, 65da066 kind-filter-single-list, 06d84e9 search-syntax-click-example); the rebase was clean and the check was run on top of all three, twice. Pushed to origin (06d84e9..26ab60c).

With the new trunk commits: kind-filter-single-list builds a kind search's query in `kind_tokens`; its tokens are filters, so `loose_text` sees no loose text in them, and a kind search with no word (Image + `*.svg`) is sorted among every match. With a kind, a lone `src/` is a folder filter and is sorted through; without one it is loose text and is not. The other two commits touch nothing here.

How it was checked. (1) Tests without the change: with the src and crates diff reverse-applied on the implementer's commit, the five controls tests and the settings test fail at the assertion that names the problem (["No Date"]; [ledger.txt, ledger] for the two largest; [b.log, c.log, a.log]; the Recents list in relevance order; created None; last_opened None) and the guard test passes; `git apply` again left the tree clean. (2) My fixes, one taken out at a time on the final code: 9 engine mutations (early return on `truncated`; no loose rule; no names rule; the fallback keeping the flag; folders not counted as reads; no read bound; the flag ignoring `truncated`; the old loose rule; loose text never) and 3 window mutations (re-run whenever cut; no direction guard; the flag never set): every one fails a test. (3) The new and changed tests 25 times (engine) and 15 times (UI) in a row: no failure. (4) A probe over 77,559 files (cargo registry sources, /usr/share, /usr/lib, /usr/include) with 111 queries, before and after the fixes; the numbers in this record are from it. It confirmed the commit message's claim: of the 30 largest matches of readme, log, error, build, main, serde, report and notes, none has the word in its name. In every one-word query the plain list has all its names with the word ahead of every other hit, and so has the wide fetch, which is what `sort_can_choose` goes by. (5) The window: five pictures of my own (columns filled; `*.txt` by Size with Results shown 8; `tax` with Results shown 4, best first and by Size, the same four items; `tax` with Results shown 2 by Size, the two largest names).

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt, and what the code does. (a) Slower typing under a sort: one pass unless a sort chooses; disk reads bounded at 5,000 per search plus Results shown for the columns. (b) Items going missing on a sort click: where a sort chooses, by design and said in the manual; elsewhere the rows are no longer touched. (c) The wrong items after a re-run, across tabs and with a search in flight: the window keeps its results best first and sorts rows itself; a sort changed while a search is on its way goes with that search (tested); a column added in another tab re-runs this tab's search (tested).

For the briefs still to come:
- result-tie-break: `sort_before_cut` needs `raw` best first and its sort is stable, so your order decides among hits the sort key can't tell apart. `cut_in_order` puts the chosen hits back best first with `hits.sort_by_key(|hit| Reverse(hit.score))` on `SearchHit`s, by the score alone: give that the same tie-break, or the answer to a sorted search is ordered differently from a plain one where scores tie. `sort_can_choose` relies on rerank putting every name that has all the words ahead of every other hit; a bonus that keeps that is fine. Your order does not make the plain list the same from run to run: see Found, not fixed.
- query-history-boost: a_best_match_opened_before_stays_in_the_list_under_a_sort opens a file with `track_open` and expects it first for the same search, with `db_dir` set. If the engine takes over the +1,000, add it before `rerank` in both passes (the plain one and the wide one go through the same code). `sort_can_choose` is what keeps a boosted file whose name lacks a word in the list; if you would rather have it sorted among the names with that file kept in, that is the place.
- live-search-results: quiet reruns go through `run_search`, which sends `result_sort` and the two read flags. Under a sort that chooses a rerun is two engine passes. `SearchStats` has a new field `sort_chooses` that every place building one must fill (a contents search: false). A rerun replaces `results`, and the plain list changes from run to run (below), so a quiet rerun will reshuffle a cut list of loose matches.
- typo-fallback-near-miss: typo-only hits have no word in their names, so a list of them says `sort_chooses: false` and is never sorted before the cut. Filter before the dedup, as `strict` does; `sort_before_cut` comes after it.
- multi-word-highlights: `into_hit(needle, ..)` is also called from `cut_in_order`, and the tests call `into_hit("", true)`, `cut_to_limit(.., "env", ..)` and `cut_in_order(.., "tax", ..)`.
- recents-walk-index: Recents rows still lack Date Created and Permissions. `FileEntry::read_metadata` fills them for a file hit; Recents has no request to ask with.
- regex-content-search: `content_search` builds a `SearchStats`; `sort_chooses` stays false there.
- back-forward-restore-search, recent-searches, smart-folder-save-and-leaks: a search's sort (`result_sort`) now changes which items a cut list holds, and still isn't saved; a restored search starts at Relevance unless you restore the sort too, and then it must be set before `run_search`.
- search-start-no-flash: a re-run for a sort change keeps `search_stats`, so the rows stay on screen and no placeholders show; `searching` is true meanwhile.

Found, not fixed:
- The plain search lists different items from run to run when many matches tie. fff-search is asked for its best 2,000 per search location and cuts among equal scores in no fixed order. In the 77,559-file tree, consecutive runs of the same search share 265 to 396 of 500 items for `index` (every file under `index.crates.io-...` matches by its path), about 300 for `bench`, 325 to 377 for `readme` (a list of names only), and `makefile` came back with 342 hits and then 429. Refresh, typing the same words again, and the retries while indexing all reshuffle such a list. It was there before this change; what this change adds is that a sort click re-runs the search where a sort chooses (the chosen list is the same each time when the wide fetch holds every match). result-tie-break orders ties after the fetch and can't fix which candidates are fetched.
- The plain list can leave out names that match. `x86`: 394 names with x86 in them and 106 path matches are listed, while 563 names match; fff-search ranks path matches above some name matches in its best 2,000, and rerank only sees what was fetched.
- Name searches can't be cancelled (left_out).
- `SearchRequest.sort` does not sort the answer; the field's doc says so, but the name invites the assumption. `/v1/find` doesn't expose it.
- A broken symlink is read through `symlink_metadata` for its row and through `metadata` for the sort's choice by Date Created, so such a file is chosen as if it had no date.
